name: flock
description: See every Claude Code session you're running as one live tree — who forked from whom, who's working, and who's waiting on you.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Flock launches terminals, which VS Code blocks in Restricted Mode.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Flock needs a real filesystem and terminals to find and launch Claude Code sessions.

colors.description: Flock brand accent used for tree icons.
Status dot for a session that is working right now.
Status dot for a session that has finished and is waiting on you — the row that wants your attention.
Status dot for a session being compacted — a hollow ring while the compaction runs, a full dot once it has finished with nothing behind it.
Row colour for a session that is over: closed, exited, or an inferred ancestor. Used by the built-in tree view, which has no other way to dim a row.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No Claude Code sessions here yet — Flock starts with a clean slate.
[Recommended Setup...](command:lineage.recommendedSetup)
A checklist of what a fresh install should turn on, with the reason on every line. You tick what you want; nothing is written until you do.
[New Project](command:lineage.newProject)
[New Claude Session](command:lineage.newSession)
A project is a name and a directory; every session running in it groups under it. Add a second directory later and each one gets a row of its own.
[Import Previous Sessions...](command:lineage.importSessions)
Sessions from before Flock — or running in some other terminal — stay off the tree until you import them, all at once or one folder at a time.
If sessions you started here are missing, set `lineage.claudeBinary` to the full path of your claude CLI.

No Claude Code sessions here yet — Flock starts with a clean slate.
[Recommended Setup...](command:lineage.recommendedSetup)
A checklist of what a fresh install should turn on, with the reason on every line. You tick what you want; nothing is written until you do.
[New Project](command:lineage.newProject)
[New Claude Session](command:lineage.newSession)
A project is a name and a directory; every session running in it groups under it. Add a second directory later and each one gets a row of its own.
[Import Previous Sessions...](command:lineage.importSessions)
Sessions from before Flock — or running in some other terminal — stay off the tree until you import them, all at once or one folder at a time.
If sessions you started here are missing, set `lineage.claudeBinary` to the full path of your claude CLI.

No AI accounts yet.
[Add Account](command:lineage.addAccount)
An account is one subscription you can launch sessions on — a Claude plan, a ChatGPT / Codex plan, an API key. Flock lists the CLIs it finds on this machine on its own; add a second login of either here. Each gets its own config directory, so you sign in once per account and never again.

Nothing is running.
[New Session](command:lineage.newSession)
This lists the commands your sessions are running right now — every `Bash` call Claude has started and not yet got back from, with a clock on each, and every background job until it finishes, which is the one thing in a Claude session that is otherwise easy to lose track of. A command that ends leaves the list.
It covers every live session on this machine that Flock lists, not just this window's. Click a row to jump to the conversation that started it.

enumDescriptions: A normal editor tab beside your files.
The terminal panel at the bottom.
An editor tab moved into its own window.
lineage.terminalLocation.markdownDescription: **Where a session opens.** An editor tab, the bottom panel, or a window of its own.

lineage.soloSession.markdownDescription: **One session tab at a time.** Focusing a session parks the others: hidden if tmux-wrapped, closed and resumable if bare. Off, because it moves tabs you laid out yourself.

enumDescriptions: A terminal Flock owns. Every verb works.
The Claude Code extension's panel. Needs that extension.
lineage.launch.mode.markdownDescription: **Who opens a conversation.** In the Claude Code extension Flock does not own the process: no tmux parking, no Close with Summary, no account pinning. A fork always opens in Flock's own terminal.

enumDescriptions: A private, invisible tmux server, whenever tmux is installed.
Bare `claude` processes. Switches close and resume them.
lineage.tmux.markdownDescription: **Keep sessions alive in tmux.** Switching away hides a session instead of closing it, and it comes back live. Needs tmux on PATH; never on Windows.

lineage.exitToShell.markdownDescription: **Leave a shell after `/exit`.** The tab stays open at a prompt, ready for `claude --resume`. Needs `#lineage.tmux#`; takes effect once every current session has ended.

enumDescriptions: The tree follows the conversation in front; `alt+left` jumps to its row.
Leave the Claude Code extension's own agent list alone.
lineage.sessionSwitching.markdownDescription: **Where you switch conversations.** With the tree as the switcher, the current conversation's row stays selected and `alt+left` over the Claude Code extension jumps to it.

lineage.fork.notifyParent.markdownDescription: **Tell the parent about a fork.** One sentence typed into the parent conversation. Costs it a turn, and only while the parent's tab is open in this window.

enumDescriptions: Compact, keep the summary, tell the parent, close.
Compact, keep the summary, close.
You type the summary. Also the fallback when compaction is refused.
No summary. The same as Close Session.
lineage.close.summaryMode.markdownDescription: **What Close with Summary does.** Compacting sends `/compact` and keeps the summary the CLI writes: one to three minutes, Claude only, tab open in this window. No summary, nothing closes.

enumDescriptions: The folder you opened. Other projects get their own windows. Needs no tmux.
No folder. Every session on the machine in one tree; open a session's window when you want its files. Nothing switches by itself.
One window switches project as you work, saving and restoring layouts. Wants tmux, and one reload (a window opened with no folder does it by itself).
lineage.mode.markdownDescription: **What a window is.** One folder per project, Flock only, or one window that follows you. **Flock: Choose Window Model…** shows what each costs.

lineage.workspaces.enabled.markdownDescription: **Workspace switcher in the status bar.** Scopes the window to one project. The notice above says what replaced it.
lineage.workspaces.enabled.markdownDeprecationMessage: Superseded by `#lineage.mode#`, and still honoured: while this is `false` and the mode is `project`, this window resolves to the **Root** (Flock only) model — which is what that pair has always actually meant. Set `#lineage.mode#` to the model you want, or run **Flock: Choose Window Model…**, which writes both; then this key can go.

lineage.workspaces.resumeSessions.markdownDescription: **Resume parked sessions on a switch.** Up to 8 per switch. Off, nothing is parked.

lineage.explorer.followProject.markdownDescription: **The Explorer follows the session.** Auto-switch only. The window must be a Flock workspace: one reload, automatic when no folder is open, otherwise **Flock: Follow the Session I Am In**.

enumDescriptions: One root: the directory you are in. The Project view lists the rest.
Every connected directory as its own root. The tree stops following you.
lineage.explorer.scope.markdownDescription: **How much of the project the Explorer shows.** Auto-switch only, with `#lineage.explorer.followProject#` on.

lineage.showForeignSessions.markdownDescription: **Show sessions started outside Flock.** Off, the tree holds only what you launched here or added yourself, and nothing else can ring the bell.

enumDescriptions: Under a row for their directory.
One by one, beside the projects.
Not shown, unless running.
lineage.unclaimedSessions.markdownDescription: **Sessions no project claims.** Hidden is ignored while you have no projects, and never hides a running session.

lineage.onlyActiveSessions.markdownDescription: **Only running sessions.** The same switch as the button in the view title.

lineage.showTokens.markdownDescription: **Token count on each row.** The context the last turn ran with, as `/context` reports it.

lineage.accounts.section.markdownDescription: **Accounts section.** One row per subscription: plan, usage, and which one new sessions use. Off moves the sidebar's buttons up onto the FLOCK header.

lineage.shells.section.markdownDescription: **Shells section.** The commands your sessions are running right now, with a clock on each. Every live session on this machine is covered, not only this window's.

enumDescriptions: Flock's own view. Rename in place on the row.
VS Code's built-in tree. Rename in a box at the top.
lineage.viewStyle.markdownDescription: **How the Sessions view is drawn.** Takes effect on the next reload.

lineage.showArchived.markdownDescription: **Every closed session on disk**, even ones this tree never knew. Not the archive: that is **Archived Sessions…** on the project row.

lineage.showPhantomRows.markdownDescription: **Debug: roster rows that are not sessions.** Exited entries and warm spares. They cannot be focused or resumed.

lineage.notifications.enabled.markdownDescription: **Green dot and bell for finished turns**, until you look at the session. Right-click a session to mute it.

lineage.notifications.popup.markdownDescription: **Also pop up a toast** with a Focus button. Off: the dots and the bell already say it.

lineage.accounts.offerSwitchAtLimit.markdownDescription: **Offer another account at the limit.** One notification when a session's five-hour window runs out, naming the account with the most room. Off: it interrupts.

lineage.runningBadge.markdownDescription: **Running count on the Flock icon.** Off: it changes every few seconds, and the tree already says it.

lineage.git.newSessionInWorktree.markdownDescription: **New sessions get their own worktree.** `+` on a project runs `git worktree add -b` on a branch named after the session. Off, `+` starts in the project directory.

lineage.git.branchPrefix.markdownDescription: **Prefix for minted branch names.** `axel/` gives `axel/flock-3`. Names you type yourself get no prefix.

lineage.git.worktreePath.markdownDescription: **Where new worktrees go.** `${repo}` and `${branch}` are filled in; a relative path sits beside the main worktree, so the default gives `~/code/app-feat-x`. Must contain `${branch}`.

lineage.git.branches.markdownDescription: **Branch rows.** A project's branches as rows, with the worktree verbs, the colours and the pull-request chip. Off: it is a lot of rows.

enumDescriptions: A line under the session: `⎇ feat/search ↑4 *`. Costs a row.
The session's name in its branch's colour. Costs nothing; says which sessions share a checkout, not which one.
lineage.git.branchDisplay.markdownDescription: **How a session shows its worktree.** Needs `#lineage.git.branches#`.

lineage.git.pullRequests.markdownDescription: **Pull request on each branch row.** The one setting that reaches the network: `gh pr list`, at most every five minutes, through your own signed-in `gh`. Flock never sees a token.

enumDescriptions: Branch, ahead/behind, and `*` for uncommitted changes.
Also the pull request: number, checks, state.
lineage.git.sessionBranchDetail.markdownDescription: **How much the branch line says.** Inline display only. The pull request needs `#lineage.git.pullRequests#`.

lineage.groupSessionsByBranch.markdownDescription: **Nest sessions under their branch.** Each branch row becomes a container with its own `+`. Projects with two or more worktrees only.

lineage.branchColors.markdownDescription: **Colours for the branch chips**, in order. Hex or theme colour ids; empty uses the Source Control Graph's colours. Colour mode only.

lineage.preview.directoryModel.markdownDescription: **Preview: branch rows per directory.** Every local branch, under the directory that is its repository, the idle ones folded into one **Branches (N)** row. Needs `#lineage.git.branches#`; inline view only.

lineage.session.closeAfterMinutes.markdownDescription: **Close idle session tabs after this many minutes.** 4320 is three days. The conversation stays as a resumable row; a busy session waits for its turn, and the tab in front and **Keep Awake** sessions are never touched. `0` turns it off.

lineage.chat.autoCloseMinutes.markdownDescription: **Close idle project chats after this many minutes.** 1440 is one day. **Chat History…** reopens one. `0` turns it off.

lineage.session.detachGraceMinutes.markdownDescription: **How long a hidden session keeps running.** Then it settles to an archived row. At most 8 run detached at once. `0` ends it within a minute.

lineage.session.reloadGraceSeconds.markdownDescription: **How long a session outlives its window.** A reload and a close look the same, so Flock waits this long for the window to come back. Keep it low.

lineage.busyStaleMinutes.markdownDescription: **When a silent busy session counts as idle.** The CLI sometimes leaves a status stuck at busy; a transcript quiet this long is drawn idle.

lineage.hooks.enabled.markdownDescription: **Read the hook event stream.** Instant updates instead of the three-second poll. The install verbs turn this on; this is the switch that makes Flock read them.

lineage.verbs.enabled.markdownDescription: **Let Claude fork from inside a session.** "Fork this session" writes a request into `~/.lineage/requests`; this switch makes Flock act on it. Nothing leaves your machine.

lineage.claudeBinary.markdownDescription: **Path to the `claude` CLI.** Empty searches PATH.

lineage.codexBinary.markdownDescription: **Path to the `codex` CLI.** Empty searches PATH and the usual install roots. Set it if VS Code does not inherit your node version manager.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Flock
walkthroughs.description: Four things worth knowing before you run six agents at once.

steps.title: The tree starts empty
steps.description:
Nothing you ran before Flock, and nothing running in another terminal, appears until you say so — and nothing rings the bell either. Two doors bring your history in.
[Open the Sessions view](command:workbench.view.extension.lineage)

steps.title: Turn on the parts that are off
steps.description:
Some of the best of Flock is off until you ask, because turning it on writes files in your home directory. The checklist asks four things — instant updates, in-session verbs, your first project, your history — says what each one writes, and you tick what you want. What a window is, and where sessions open, live in the gear and are asked once, when they become real.
[Recommended Setup...](command:lineage.recommendedSetup)

steps.title: Start one from the tree
steps.description:
Press + on any project row. The session appears immediately with its name selected — type over it or press Enter. No dialog.
[New Claude Session](command:lineage.newSession)

steps.title: Watch the right edge
steps.description: Amber means working. Red means finished and not yet seen — like an unread message, it clears when you look. Purple is a compaction: a ring while it runs, a dot once it has settled. Everything else stays blank on purpose.
